items.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, and the spy case behind it is wobbling
items.summary: Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, @aleabitoreddit reported Thursday, and @DeepValueBagger notes he keeps no advisory, board or honorary role. Within hours the case against him softened: citing CNN, @KobeissiLetter reports that US intelligence officials say the evidence on Alice Huang does not prove she was spying for China, with ODNI officials calling that characterization "over-torqued" and the CIA "not yet convinced." Per WIRED, an internal Nvidia post urging the board to reinstate him has drawn more than 1,600 comments, most in support. @GavinSBaker: the board should have waited for its own investigation to finish.
items.short: Huang is out at Nvidia; officials now doubt the spy claims and employees want him back.

items.headline: Researcher: Chinese labs' newest models were trained on export-barred Blackwell chips
items.summary: @willdepue says model weights carry a fingerprint of the GPU that initialized them, and that after searching more than six trillion chip-layout and seed combinations he matched six Chinese models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3, to Nvidia Blackwell systems, four to Grace Blackwell racks. He says a B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash's starting weights bit for bit while an H100 matched none, and estimates the largest runs used 2,000-3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. He says researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic independently verified the result.
items.short: A weight-forensics study ties six Chinese models to Blackwell hardware.

items.author: Paul Millerd
items.text:
There's a weird thing I've noticed on social media wher entrepreneurs and creators always recommend building up a side income before leaving your job 

Except almost none of them actually did this!

I think what's going on is that this piece of wisdom just does much better in an algorithmic feed 

It appeals not only to the people that want to quit their job, but also the people that think a lot of people who are doing their own thing are naive and should stay in their jobs

If you say something like, “hey, you should just take a leap and bet on yourself and see where it goes, and not having a plan is okay”

Not only do the people that want to dunk on the self-employed ignore it, but a good majority of people that want to quit their job ignore it too because they want to buy into the fantasy that you can plan such a life transition 

I suspect woo advice on taking an unconventional path is the right advice 

But algorithmic feeds don't optimize for usefulness. They optimize for fantasies and projections   

Quit your job, people, and embrace the beautiful adventure of doing work that calls to you! 

Embrace potential failure. Be okay with doing whatever work can fund the journey. Return to your job if you have to

items.author: Gavin Baker
items.text:
Well-meaning, patriotic China “Hawks” who are not AI/HW experts are putting American national security at risk.

China had *zero* chance of ever catching America in AI with the export strategy that Jensen supported. Their labs would have continued training using less powerful American GPUs which meant American labs would have always been ahead given scaling laws. And in the event of a conflict, we could have simply turned off all the Southeast Asian clouds.

Simply stated, in AI terms, America had machine guns and we were giving China muskets to prevent them from developing their own machine gun variants. 

Given that it looks like the China “Hawks” will get their preferred policy, China will likely soon have a chance of catching America in AI by going down an alternate, less power-efficient AI hardware path. They almost certainly would not have gone down this path if less powerful GPUs were still available in China and via Southeast Asian clouds.

And it will be a much less stable world if China pulls even or ahead of America in AI after developing their own alternative AI HW and gives this technology to Russia, Iran and North Korea. And all of this will be possible if the China “Hawks” get their preferred policy.

items.headline: An enzyme that drives tissue ageing without inflammation
items.summary: Aged mice engineered to lack the enzyme granzyme K had better heart and liver function, less kidney damage and less age-related liver scarring, Nature reports on a study in Immunity. Drugs that lower the protein might one day slow ageing in tissues without weakening immune defences.
items.short: Mice without granzyme K aged with healthier hearts, livers and kidneys.

items.headline: Review: fitness predicts a longer life more strongly than diet does
items.summary: A review in Mayo Clinic Proceedings by ASU's Glenn Gaesser and Kaiser Permanente's Robert Sallis found physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness more strongly tied to lower mortality than diet quality. Meta-analyses linked 11,000-16,000 steps a day to 45-67% lower all-cause mortality than 2,000-5,000, and high fitness largely offset the excess risk of a poorer diet.
items.short: Steps and fitness beat diet quality as predictors of longevity.

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a parcel is marked Express, it has a red sticker.
items.explanation: Express could hide something that breaks the rule; No sticker breaks it if the other side turns out to be Express. Red sticker can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and Standard isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.

across.clue: The side of something that is sheltered from the wind
Formally making a person known to another or to the public
The seed of the cereal grass

down.clue: A hit that flies straight out from the batter
An item inserted in a written record
Switch from a higher to a lower beam
A state of decay usually accompanied by an offensive odor
